 Judgment

MFA No.202045/2023 is filed by the appellant- Insurance Company aggrieved by the order dated 29.08.2022 passed in MVC No.345/2020 on the file of II NC: 2023:KHC-K:8615 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200088 of 2023 Additional Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Bidar, by which the Tribunal while partly allowing the claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 had granted a compensation of Rs.5,41,709/- with interest at the rate of 9% p.a., while MFA Crob. No.
200088/2023 is filed by the cross objector/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.
2.

entities.text: Additional Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accident in question that arose on 03.07.2020 involving a motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-38-Q-4829 which was insured with the appellant- Insurance Company, resulting in injuries to the claimant who was a pillion rider of the said motorcycle is not in dispute.

The claimant/cross objector who was working as a police constable at the time of accident claimed compensation in a Acko Gen. Ins. Co Ltd vs Rachappa And Anr on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151700148/
3 sum of Rs.11,00,000/-.

entities.text: Acko Gen. Ins. Co Ltd vs Rachappa And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Tribunal considering the factual aspect of the matter had awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,41,709/- as under;
"Rs.2,02,909/- (Rs.1,23,909+ Rs.29,000+ Rs.50,000) towards medical expenses and Rs.1,00,000/- towards notional compensation due to injuries sustained by the claimant.

In addition to NC: 2023:KHC-K:8615 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200088 of 2023 that, the tribunal has also awarded Rs.2,82,509/- towards medical and hospital bills and has also awarded interest at the rate of 9% p.a. on the said compensation."
3.

Adverting to the above, Smt. Preethi Patil Melkundi learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance company submits that there is no dispute with regard to grant of compensation of Rs.2,02,909/-
towards medical bills and Rs.1,00,000/- towards the compensation due to the injuries sustained by the claimant.
However, there is no justification or basis for the Tribunal awarding a sum of Rs.2,82,509/- under the heading medical and hospital bills in the absence of any material evidence in this respect.
She also submits that the claimant in his evidence has deposed that he has not availed any medical reimbursement from the department and that he has not produced any certificate in that regard.
She further submits that in the absence of any grounds urged and substantiated the tribunal was not justified in awarding the excess payment of Rs.2,82,509/-.
Hence, seeks for allowing of the appeal.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:8615 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200088 of 2023 4.

Smt. Patil Shanthabai Subhash, learned counsel for the respondent/cross objector on the other hand submits that the tribunal has not awarded compensation under the heads of loss of earning during treatment and laid up period, loss of amenities, attendant charges and other heads.

She submits that injured claimant was working as a police constable at the time of accident and that now he is retired from the service and that he also requires future medical treatment and Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under other heads.
Hence, apart from seeking dismissal of the appeal she also seeks for enhancement of compensation.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
6.
Except production of medical bills for a sum of Rs.2,02,909/- the claimant/cross objector has not produced any other evidence.
The said amount of Rs.2,02,909/- has been awarded by the Tribunal.
That NC: 2023:KHC-K:8615 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200088 of 2023 apart the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards injuries sustained by the claimant.

As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company there is no reasoning or justification by the tribunal in awarding Rs.2,82,509/- under the head medical and hospital bills, as the same has been awarded in a sum of Rs.2,02,909/-.
7. However, it needs to be seen that injured claimant was treated for a period of 117 days and he has sustained following injuries as per wound certificate-Ex.

entities.text: Acko Gen. Ins. Co Ltd vs Rachappa And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Leg # of R.T Tibia Fibuls DOD 10.07.2020 Caused with hard ogc and grievous in nature."

8. In that view of the matter and taking into consideration of the over all facts situation of the case,
this court is of the considered view that instead of Rs.1,00,000/- granted by the tribunal under this head compensation due to injuries the same may be enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/-.
Thus the claimants would be entitled for NC: 2023:KHC-K:8615 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200088 of 2023 a total compensation of Rs.4,02,909/- instead of Rs.5,41,709/-.
The interest awarded by the tribunal at the rate of 9% is reduced to 6% p.a. on the aforesaid compensation amount.

9. In that view of the matter, the appeal in MFA No.202045/2023 filed by the appellant-Insurance company is partly allowed and MFA Crob.No.20008/2023 filed by the claimant/cross objector is dismissed.
10. Any amount in deposit be transmitted to the tribunal along with trial Court records.
The aforesaid modified compensation amount shall be paid to the injured claimant within a period of six weeks from the date of the receipt of the certified copy of this order.

If there is any excess amount,
the same may be refunded to the appellant-Insurance company.

Sd/-
